title: Signed spin precession under a declared field model
question: How does a signed gyromagnetic ratio predict cyclic and angular precession frequencies?
answerPreview: The moment-field model gives signed cyclic frequency f = (gamma/2 pi)B and signed angular frequency omega = 2 pi f. With transverse phase phi = -omega t, positive omega rotates clockwise and negative omega counterclockwise in the declared x-y view.
summary: Keep signed cyclic gamma/(2 pi), signed angular omega, the explicit 2 pi conversion, and the separate phase sign phi = -omega t distinct while bounding the calculation to free-particle moment-field phase evolution without relaxation, shielding, material, or detector claims.

guidedBlocks.title: Keep sign, cycles, and radians separate
body: The catalog stores gamma/(2 pi) in hertz per tesla. For a positive field magnitude along positive z, f = (gamma/(2 pi))B keeps the catalog sign.
Angular frequency is omega = 2 pi f. The factor 2 pi converts cycles to radians exactly once; f and omega are not numerically interchangeable.
The transverse projection uses phi = -omega t, x = cos(phi), and y = sin(phi). Positive omega therefore rotates clockwise and negative omega counterclockwise in the declared x-y view.

caveats: Changing the axis or phase convention can change the verbal rotation-sense label.

guidedBlocks.title: A rotating marker is model output
body: The visualizer evolves a unit-circle phase marker under a static uniform field and a free-particle gyromagnetic ratio.
It does not model longitudinal or transverse relaxation, shielding, field gradients, interactions, anisotropy, material response, or detector signals.
A displayed frequency is therefore a calculated reference under the moment-field model, not an observed resonance or a material measurement.
caveats: No relaxation time, linewidth, amplitude, noise, or uncertainty is calculated.

guidedBlocks.title: The response starts from a moment-field model
body: The declared model uses magnetic moment mu = gamma S and interaction Hamiltonian H = -mu dot B.
For a static field along positive z, define signed angular frequency omega = gamma B and transverse phase phi(t) = -omega t in the declared x-y projection.
The catalog ratio already contains particle-specific magnetic information; the activity does not derive gamma from particle geometry.
guidedBlocks.sourceRevision: CODATA 2022; OpenStax University Physics Volume 3, 2016 web edition accessed 2026-07-27; Tour contract 2026-07-26
guidedBlocks.sourceLocator: Signed ratios; OpenStax sections 8.2-8.3; Chapter 9 moment-field model
caveats: The gyromagnetic ratio is an input, not a prediction of this activity.

technicalBlocks.title: Signed phase and positive period carry different information
body: The signed phase is phi(t) = -omega t. It decreases for positive gamma and increases for negative gamma under the declared positive-z and x-y convention.
The cyclic magnitude is |f| and the period is T = 1/|f|, so period remains positive even for the electron and negative muon.
The bounded sample table evaluates cos(phi) and sin(phi) at 2 through 128 points including both time endpoints.
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: Signed phase, magnitude, period, and sampling definitions
caveats: Samples are visualization coordinates, not successive detector readings.

technicalBlocks.title: Free-particle gamma is not a material resonance model
body: The proton entry is an unshielded free-proton value. Chemical shielding would alter a material-specific nuclear magnetic resonance frequency.
Electron spin resonance in matter can require an anisotropic g-tensor, and composite particles can require context-specific moment corrections.
Relaxation, coupling, line shape, field calibration, and measurement uncertainty must be supplied before a model frequency can be compared with an observed signal.
technicalBlocks.sourceLocator: Free-particle ratio scope and Chapter 9 limits
caveats: No shielding, composite, or environmental correction is available in this engine.

equationSteps.label: Cyclic and angular frequency
equationSteps.expression: f = (gamma/(2 pi)) B; omega = 2 pi f = gamma B
equationSteps.explanation: The catalog value is signed gamma/(2 pi) in Hz per tesla. Multiplication by 2 pi converts signed cycles per second to signed radians per second.
equationSteps.sourceLocator: gamma/(2 pi) entries and frequency conversion
caveats: B is a positive magnitude along positive z in the activity convention.

equationSteps.label: Bounded phase visualization
equationSteps.expression: phi(t) = -omega t; x = cos(phi); y = sin(phi); T = 1/|f|
equationSteps.explanation: The explicit minus sign maps signed angular frequency to marker direction under the declared projection, while the reciprocal period uses frequency magnitude and remains positive.
equationSteps.sourceLocator: Phase, unit-circle, and period output definitions
caveats: The marker is not a classical picture of a measured spin trajectory.

checkpoints.prompt: A free proton at 1 T has f about 42.58 MHz. What is the angular-frequency magnitude?
checkpoints.explanation: omega = 2 pi f, so 42.58 million cycles per second corresponds to about 267.5 million radians per second.

caveats: This authored answer is not a measured resonance.

checkpoints.prompt: Under the activity phase convention, what does a negative signed gamma change?
checkpoints.explanation: The signed angular frequency reverses phase direction. With phi = -omega t, negative gamma gives positive phase advance and counterclockwise rotation; the period still uses |f| and remains positive.
